markup_blocks.heading: Paragraph
markup_blocks.description:
A paragraph is the most basic block structure in a doc comment.
Any plain text that is not part of another command is treated as a paragraph.
Consecutive lines of text are merged into a single paragraph; a blank line starts a new one.

The `@details` command is an explicit way to begin the detailed description section, but in practice you rarely need it -- any text after the brief summary is already treated as detail paragraphs.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The paragraph body. Plain prose is detected automatically; `@details` begins the detailed-description section explicitly.

markup_blocks.heading: Heading
markup_blocks.description:
The `@par` command creates a named heading (subsection) inside a doc comment.
The text on the same line as `@par` becomes the heading title; subsequent lines form the body of that section.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The heading text, on the same line as `@par`. If omitted, no heading is emitted.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The section body, on the lines after `@par`.

markup_blocks.heading: List
markup_blocks.description:
Creates an unordered (bulleted) list inside a doc comment.
You can use the Javadoc/Doxygen `@li` command, its alias `@arg`, or Markdown-style dash bullets (`- `).
All three syntaxes produce the same list structure.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The text of one list item.

markup_blocks.heading: Table
markup_blocks.description:
Creates a table inside a doc comment using HTML table markup.
MrDocs parses standard HTML `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>` elements and converts them to a table in the output format.

markup_blocks.heading: Code Block
markup_blocks.description:
Inserts a block of preformatted code into the documentation.
Everything between the opening and closing tags is preserved verbatim, including whitespace and indentation.

`@code` and `@verbatim` produce the same output.
Use `@code` for source code and `@verbatim` for other preformatted text, though MrDocs treats them identically.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Optional language hint for syntax highlighting, e.g. `cpp`.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The verbatim source between the opening command and `@endcode`/`@endverbatim`.

markup_blocks.heading: Admonitions
markup_blocks.description:
Admonition commands wrap a paragraph in a callout block.
The five kinds differ in urgency:

* `@note` -- supplementary information the reader should be aware of.
* `@tip` -- a helpful suggestion or best practice.
* `@important` -- information critical to correct usage.
* `@warning` -- something that could lead to unexpected behavior if ignored.
* `@caution` -- something that could cause data loss, security issues, or other serious problems.

The text following the command becomes the body of the admonition block.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The admonition body.

markup_blocks.heading: Quote
markup_blocks.description:
The AST defines a Quote node, but no parser path produces it yet.
When that lands, it will hold a blockquote inside a doc comment.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The quoted text; prefix each line with `>`.

markup_blocks.heading: Thematic Break
markup_blocks.description:
The AST defines a ThematicBreak node, but no parser path produces it yet.
When that lands, it will render as a horizontal rule between doc-comment sections.

markup_blocks.heading: Definition List
markup_blocks.description:
The AST defines a DefinitionList node, but no parser path produces it yet.
When that lands, it will hold a definition list of term-description pairs.

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: The term being defined.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.description: A definition, on a line prefixed with `:`.

markup_blocks.heading: Footnote Definition
markup_blocks.description:
Defines the body of a footnote, matched to references by its label.
Start the paragraph with the label after a caret in square brackets, then a colon and the footnote text.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The footnote identifier that references point to.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The footnote body.

markup_blocks.heading: Math Block
markup_blocks.description:
A standalone display math expression on its own line.
A paragraph that is only `$$...$$`, or a `\f[...\f]` Doxygen block, becomes a math block; inline `$...$` and `\f$...\f$` stay in the surrounding text as a Math span.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A standalone LaTeX math expression.

metadata_blocks.heading: Summary
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@brief` command marks its content as the brief description (summary) of the documented symbol.
The first sentence of a doc comment is automatically treated as the brief, so you only need `@brief` when you want to override that behavior or when the automatic detection does not capture what you intend.

`@short` is an alias for `@brief`.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The brief, one-sentence summary of the symbol.

metadata_blocks.heading: Parameters
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@param` command documents a function parameter.
Write one `@param` per parameter you want to describe.
The parameter name follows the command, and everything after it is the description.

An optional direction indicator can appear in square brackets between `@param` and the parameter name to specify how data flows through the parameter.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: Optional parameter direction.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The function parameter being documented; must match the signature.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description of the parameter.

metadata_blocks.heading: Template Parameters
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@tparam` command documents a template parameter.
It works like `@param`, but for type, non-type, and template-of-template parameters.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The template parameter; must match the template declaration.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description of the template parameter.

metadata_blocks.heading: Returns
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@return` command documents the return value of a function.
All three spellings are equivalent.
You can use multiple `@return` commands when a function returns a composite value and you want to describe each part separately.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description of the return value.

metadata_blocks.heading: Exceptions
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@throw` command documents an exception that a function may throw.
All three spellings are equivalent.
The exception type follows the command, and the rest of the line (and continuation lines) describe when or why the exception is thrown.

parameters.name: exception
parameters.description: The exception type that may be thrown, e.g. `std::invalid_argument`.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: When and why the exception is thrown.

metadata_blocks.heading: Preconditions
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@pre` command documents a precondition that must hold before calling the function.
You can use multiple `@pre` commands to list several preconditions; each one renders as a separate bullet in a "Preconditions" section.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A condition that must hold before the call.

metadata_blocks.heading: Postconditions
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@post` command documents a postcondition that is guaranteed after the function returns successfully.
Like `@pre`, you can use multiple `@post` commands to list several postconditions; each renders as a separate bullet in a "Postconditions" section.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A condition guaranteed after the call.

metadata_blocks.heading: See-also
metadata_blocks.description:
The `@see` command adds an entry to the "See also" section of the documented symbol.
The argument is parsed as inline content, so you can include cross-references, links, or plain text.
Multiple `@see` commands produce multiple entries.

`@sa` is a Doxygen-compatible alias for `@see`.

parameters.name: references
parameters.description: The text shown in the See Also section. Typically references to related symbols, but parsed as an ordinary paragraph.

metadata_blocks.note: `@see` looks special, but its argument is just an ordinary paragraph. MrDocs does not auto-link names inside it (Doxygen's documentation is misleading on this point). To link to a symbol, use `@ref` inside the paragraph.

metadata_blocks.heading: Relates
metadata_blocks.description: Declares that the documented free function is logically related to (or a member of) the specified class or struct. MrDocs stores each target in the symbol's `relates` field and renders it under Non-Member Functions. `@related`, `@relatedalso`, and `@relatesalso` are aliases for `@relates`; `@memberof` behaves the same way.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The class or struct this free function is related to.

metadata_blocks.heading: Function Object
metadata_blocks.description: Marks a `constexpr` variable as an https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/algorithm/ranges#Algorithm_function_objects[Algorithm Function Object (AFO)^] (the niebloid pattern: a callable object that stands in for a function). Place the command on the variable or on its function-object record; it never goes on `operator()`. MrDocs then documents the variable as a function whose signature and text come from the record's `operator()` overloads, falling back to the variable's own doc comment when `operator()` is undocumented. The record's own doc comment is not used. With `auto-function-objects` enabled (the default) a variable whose type has only `operator()` overloads is detected automatically, so the command is needed only when the type has extra public members that defeat detection. `@functor` is an alias for `@functionobject`.
metadata_blocks.note: Document the `operator()`, not the variable or the record: that is where MrDocs takes the AFO's signature and description from.

metadata_blocks.heading: See Below
metadata_blocks.description: Marks the symbol so its synopsis renders as `/* see below */` instead of the full declaration, for interfaces whose exact form is unspecified.

metadata_blocks.heading: Implementation Defined
metadata_blocks.description: Marks the symbol as implementation-defined, so its details are hidden from the generated documentation.

inline_formatting.heading: Emphasis
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content in italic (emphasized) style.
Use `*` or `_` around the emphasized text.
The Doxygen commands `@a`, `@e`, and `@em` emphasize the single word that follows them.

parameters.name: word
parameters.description: The word to emphasize (command form). The Markdown/HTML forms wrap a span of text.

inline_formatting.heading: Strong
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content in bold (strong) style.
Use `**` or `__` around the bold text.
The Doxygen commands `@b` and `@strong` bold the single word that follows them.

parameters.name: word
parameters.description: The word to render bold (command form). The Markdown/HTML forms wrap a span of text.

inline_formatting.heading: Code Span
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content in a monospace code font, inline within the surrounding text.
Markdown-style backtick delimiters wrap the text to be rendered as code.
The Doxygen commands `@c` and `@p` apply code formatting to the single word that follows them.
The HTML `<code>` tag is also recognized.

parameters.name: word
parameters.description: The word to render as inline code (command form). The Markdown/HTML forms wrap a span of text.

inline_formatting.heading: Strikethrough
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content with a horizontal line through the middle, for deleted or deprecated text.
Wrap the text in double tildes (`~~`).

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to strike through.

inline_formatting.heading: Highlight
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content with a highlighted background, drawing attention to specific words or phrases.
Markdown-style double equals signs (`==`) wrap the text.
The HTML `<mark>` tag is also recognized.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to highlight.

inline_formatting.heading: Superscript
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content as superscript, positioned above the baseline.
Use for footnote markers, exponents, and ordinal indicators.
Wrap the text in carets (`^`).

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to raise as superscript.

inline_formatting.heading: Subscript
inline_formatting.description:
Renders its content as subscript, positioned below the baseline.
Use for chemical formulas, mathematical indices, and similar notation.
Wrap the text in single tildes (`~`).

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to lower as subscript.

math.heading: Math
math.description:
Renders a mathematical expression.
Single dollar signs (`$...$`) produce an inline math span that flows within surrounding text; double dollar signs (`$$...$$`) produce a display math block on its own line.
The Doxygen delimiters `\f$...\f$` (inline) and `\f[...\f]` (display) are also recognized. Prefer them when the surrounding code is compiled with `-Wdocumentation`, since Clang parses them as known commands whereas `$...$` bodies can trip `-Wdocumentation-unknown-command`.
The content between the delimiters is treated as a literal math expression and is not parsed for Markdown or other formatting.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A LaTeX math expression; `$...$` inline, `$$...$$` display.

links_and_images.heading: Link
links_and_images.description:
Creates a hyperlink to an external URL.
The Markdown form puts the visible text in square brackets and the URL in parentheses.
The HTML form uses an `<a>` tag with an `href` attribute.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The link text.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The destination URL.

links_and_images.heading: Image
links_and_images.description: Embeds an image inline. The Markdown form is an exclamation mark, alt text in square brackets, then the source path in parentheses. The HTML form uses an `` tag with `src` and `alt` attributes. Both forms map to the same node, so pick whichever reads better. The Doxygen `@image` command is not supported, because it names a single output format and MrDocs renders every format from one model.

parameters.name: src
parameters.description: Path or URL of the image.

parameters.name: alt
parameters.description: Alternate text shown when the image cannot be displayed.

cross_references.heading: Cross-reference
cross_references.description:
Creates a cross-reference to another documented symbol.
The `@ref` command takes a symbol name (optionally namespace-qualified) and produces a link to that symbol's documentation page.
Qualified names use `::` separators (e.g., `@ref A::f1`, `@ref ::A::f1`).
Operator names are supported (e.g., `@ref F::operator+`).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Qualified name of the symbol to link to.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Optional display text for the link.

cross_references.heading: Footnote Reference
cross_references.description:
Marks a superscript reference to a footnote, linking to the matching Footnote Definition.
Write the label after a caret inside square brackets. Any string works as the label; it just has to match the definition.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The identifier of the footnote definition to reference.

copy_directives.heading: Copy
copy_directives.description: Copy documentation from another symbol. `@copydoc` copies the whole doc comment (brief, description, and every metadata block); `@copybrief` copies only the brief; `@copydetails` copies only the detailed description. Useful for overloads, redeclarations, and wrappers that share documentation with another symbol.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The symbol whose documentation to copy.

line_breaks.heading: Line Break
line_breaks.description:
The `
` HTML tag marks a hard line break inside inline content. MrDocs accepts both `
` and the self-closing `
`. The visible rendering is still being refined: the parser consumes the tag without emitting an explicit line-break element yet.

line_breaks.heading: Soft Break
line_breaks.description:
The AST defines a SoftBreak node, but no parser path produces it yet. A soft break is a line break that renderers may collapse to a space, in contrast to the hard `
` break.
